t: Find the Width of Columns of a Grid
o: For each column, find the maximum string length among its integers, counting an extra character for the minus sign on negatives. E.g., in [[-15,1,3],[15,7,12],[5,6,-2]], column 0 has max length 3 (from -15), column 1 max 1, column 2 max 2. Constraints are tiny (100x100), so any direct simulation works.
k: Length of x is len(str(x)); negatives add one for '-'.
Just iterate column-wise and take the max.

a.i: Convert each number to a string and take the maximum length per column. Trivially correct and within constraints.
s: For each column c, scan every row r.
Compute str(grid[r][c]).length and track the maximum.
Append the maximum to the answer array.

a.i: Avoid string conversion: digits(x) = 1 + floor(log10(|x|)) for x != 0, else 1; add 1 if negative. Same complexity, slightly faster constant factor.
s: Write helper len(x): handle 0 as 1; otherwise floor(log10(abs(x))) + 1, plus 1 if x < 0.
Apply per cell as in Approach 1.

w: Prefer the string-conversion approach — fewer edge cases than floating-point log10 (which can misbehave near powers of 10). Watch out for single-cell grids and all-negative columns. This problem rarely gets follow-ups; mention that for huge inputs you could compute widths per diagonal of magnitude instead.
